title: Slideomatic Field Guide
subtitle: Make a useful deck fast. Keep the weird bits that help.

image.alt: Blur album cover in warm orange motion
Colorful collage materials on a table

headline: This is the quick tour, not a rulebook
body: Slideomatic is for rough ideas, quick talks, client notes, band plans, class decks, launch rambles, and anything else that needs slides without the 42-button panic panel.
Move with **arrow keys** on desktop or swipe on touch screens. Press **E** to open the edit drawer and change the slide in front of you.
Everything starts local in your browser. Nothing needs an account. Export when you want a backup, share when you want another human to see it.

headline: Make one slide, then make the next one

pillars.title: Open
pillars.text: Start with a blank deck or duplicate a guide/demo deck when you want training wheels.

pillars.title: Edit
pillars.text: Press **E**. Change the headline, body, layout, image, theme, or notes without leaving the deck.

pillars.title: Add
pillars.text: Use **Slide Type** in the drawer, pick a layout, then hit **Add Slide**. Keep going until the shape appears.

pillars.title: Ship
pillars.text: Use **Share**, **Download JSON**, or **Download PDF** when the deck is ready to leave the nest.

headline: Press **E** and the workbench slides in
body: The edit drawer is where the deck becomes yours. It uses compact sections instead of a giant control wall.

**Theme** changes the whole deck mood. **Slide Type** swaps or adds layouts. **Content** edits the words. **Images** handles uploads, replacements, and AI assist. **Actions** covers save, duplicate, delete, JSON, and PDF.
Most text boxes also have a **Mic** button. Talk messy, get clean prompt text back. It removes the um/uh/like fog before it lands in the field.

headline: Autosave is on your side
body: Decks autosave to this browser as you work. If you close the tab and come back, your local draft should still be waiting.
Big change? Duplicate the slide first. Then wreck the copy with confidence.
For proper backup, download JSON. For humans who just need the deck, use **Share**. For print/email land, export **PDF**.

left.headline: Pick the shape
left.body: Standard for explaining, split for comparisons, quote for emphasis, gallery for visual rhythm, grid for lists or swatches, image for full-screen impact.

right.headline: Then make it yours
right.body: Change the type later if the idea outgrows the slide. A deck is allowed to be a little alive while you build it.

headline: Use pictures when words get tired
body: Drag in your own images, paste from the clipboard, or leave an empty image slot and let the AI/image helpers kick in.

headline: Fonts change the temperature
body: Use the drawer or JSON to change a slide's `font`. Keep it readable, but do not let readable become boring by accident.

caption: Images can be uploaded, pasted, generated, replaced, or kept local-only until you export a JSON backup.

headline: Press **T** when the vibe gets stale
body: **T** randomizes the deck's look. Some rolls are beautiful. Some are cursed. Both are information.
Open **Theme** in the edit drawer for presets, saved themes, AI theme prompts, and the SomaFM toggle.
If a theme almost works, save it before you keep rolling. Future you has enough problems.

image.alt: Riso chameleon mid color-change on a paint swatch wheel

headline: Grids are for scanning, comparing, and choosing
The AI stuff is there when you want turbo
body: Press **S** to add a Gemini key. The settings modal links straight to Google AI Studio's API key page: create a key, paste it in, save, test.
Type **666** or **696969** when you are not focused in a text field to open the cheat console. It can generate one slide or a rough starter deck from a prompt.
Treat AI output like a sketch, not gospel. Keep the useful bits, delete the soggy bits, make it sound like a person.

image.alt: Friendly robot painting a slide, made with the same AI image feature

headline: The keyboard is optional, but nice
body: **E** = edit drawer. **T** = random theme. **O** = overview. **I** = slide index. **N** = speaker notes.
**D** downloads JSON. **U** uploads JSON. **S** opens settings. **?** shows the full cheat sheet.
**Shift + Arrow** skips five slides. **Alt/Option + Arrow Right** duplicates the current slide.

headline: Pick the right way to move the deck

pillars.title: Local draft
pillars.text: Fastest while building. Lives in this browser under `slideomatic_deck_overrides:*`.

pillars.title: Share link
pillars.text: Best for text-light decks. Opening the link makes a local copy for the viewer.

pillars.title: JSON
pillars.text: Best backup. Keeps slides and theme together, and handles image-heavy decks better than a URL.

pillars.title: PDF
pillars.text: Best for email, print, and people who do not want to learn what JSON is today.

quote: Make the deck useful first. Make it gorgeous on pass two.

headline: Treat this like a sketchbook with a share button
body: Duplicate this guide, tear it apart, swap in your own content, and see what breaks in a fun way.
Open the drawer with **E**, pick a slide type, start typing. The blank page is less scary once it has one bad sentence on it.
Keep it human. Keep it moving. Export before you get too attached.
